name: Double Sir (Court Piece)
description: Double Sir (also known as Double Sar or Double Sir-Bandi) is a popular and strategic variant of Court Piece (Rang) played extensively in India and Pakistan. It is a trickndtaking game for four players in fixed partnerships. The defining feature of Double Sir is that a player can only capture tricks from the table if they win two consecutive tricks, adding a layered tactical challenge to standard whist-style play.

content.text: Double Sir (also known as Double Sar or Double Sir-Bandi) is a popular and strategic variant of Court Piece (Rang) played extensively in India and Pakistan. It is a trickndtaking game for four players in fixed partnerships. The defining feature of Double Sir is that a player can only capture tricks from the table if they win two consecutive tricks, adding a layered tactical challenge to standard whist-style play.
Double Sir is a regional evolution of the classic 'Court Piece' (or Rang), which traces its roots to 19thndcentury Whist. It is particularly associated with the Punjab region and North India.
Standard 52ndcard deck. Aces are high (A, K, Q, J, 10... 2).
Dealer is chosen by lot. Dealer deals 5 cards to each player. The player to the dealer's right (the 'Trump Caller') chooses the trump suit. Then the dealer deals the remaining cards in batches of 4.

items.text: No pick-up for first two tricks: A player who wins the first two tricks cannot pick them up; a player who wins the second and third tricks can pick up the three tricks as usual.
No pick-up for 11th and 12th: A player who wins the 11th and 12th tricks cannot pick up the tricks from the table, making it harder to escape a court.
Goon court counts 10: Some play that a goon court (dealer's team wins every trick) counts as 10 courts rather than three.
